audit.whatIsWrong: mid says 'Do not use Pillar offensively here or he Searing Charges right through it', and wants.you[2] tells the player to 'Use Pillar of Ice to block Ornn's retreat after he blows Bellows Breath'. spikes[0] also suggests using Pillar on his ultimate's second hit.
audit.why: Searing Charge does not go through terrain — it detonates on it. Riot: 'If Ornn collides with terrain while charging, the impact creates a shockwave around him which deals damage and knocks up enemies.' Pillar of Ice creates impassable terrain. So placing a pillar near Ornn does not fail to stop him, it actively arms him: it hands him the wall his own Volcanic Rupture normally has to build first. The advice is right that Pillar is dangerous here and wrong about every part of the reason, which means the player who follows the stated logic ('he goes through it anyway, so it does nothing') will keep casting it.
audit.corrected: Searing Charge knocks up when Ornn collides with TERRAIN, and Pillar of Ice is terrain — a pillar near him is the wall he needs, so hold it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ornn.json (E Searing Charge, cd 14/13.5/13/12.5/12, terrain + knockup)
champ-data/_kits/trundle.json (E Pillar of Ice, impassable terrain)

audit.whatIsWrong: Volcanic Rupture is named eight times across both layers as a source of 'brittle' and as a 'wall-knockup setup', and the thing it actually creates is never stated.
audit.why: Riot: 'Ornn slams the ground, sending out a fissure dealing damage and slowing enemies hit. After a small delay, a MAGMA PILLAR forms at the end location.' The pillar is the point — it is the terrain Searing Charge then charges into for the knockup. Naming it turns 'wall-knockup setup' into an instruction: watch where the fissure ends, because that is where the wall appears and where the charge will detonate. It is also 9/8.5/8/7.5/7 at 800 range, and Bellows Breath — the actual brittle source — is 12/11.5/11/10.5/10 and only its FINAL gout applies Brittle, so walking out through the front of the breath avoids it.
audit.corrected: Volcanic Rupture's fissure leaves a magma pillar at its end point, 9s at rank 1 from 800 — that pillar is the terrain Searing Charge detonates against. Brittle comes from Bellows Breath's FINAL gout, on 12s.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ornn.json (Q Volcanic Rupture, cd 9/8.5/8/7.5/7 range 800, terrain; W Bellows Breath, cd 12/11.5/11/10.5/10; E Searing Charge)

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown appears anywhere in either layer. mid tells the player to wait until 'his R is on cooldown' and to 'immediately chain R' without either number.
audit.why: Call of the Forge God is 140/120/100 and Subjugate is 120/100/80 — Trundle's ultimate is back twenty seconds sooner at every rank, which is the mechanical reason the entry's claim that level 6 'flips the match in your favour for the rest of the game' is true. Without it the claim reads as optimism. The ultimate's structure also matters: the first pass 'damages, slows and makes Brittle', and only the recast — Ornn charging into his own elemental to redirect it — knocks up. So there is one knockup to survive, not two, and it arrives on his second input.
audit.corrected: Call of the Forge God 140/120/100 against Subjugate 120/100/80 — yours is back twenty seconds sooner at every rank. The first pass brittles and slows; only the recast knocks up.

audit.whatIsWrong: Living Forge is absent from both layers. late calls Ornn 'the best possible target for your ultimate' and whys[6] calls him 'the richest Subjugate target on the map' without saying why.
audit.why: Living Forge gives Ornn 'an additional bonus Armor and Magic Resist from ALL sources', so every resistance item he buys is worth more on him than on anyone else. Subjugate takes a percentage of Health, Armor and Magic Resistance, so the passive that makes him hard to kill is the same passive that makes him the largest payout in the game for Trundle's ultimate. That is the mechanism behind the entry's central late-game claim and it was never stated.
audit.corrected: Living Forge gives him extra Armor and MR from every source — which is exactly why Subjugate's percentage pays more off Ornn than off anyone else.

audit.whatIsWrong: win[6] reads Ornn while whys[6] under it says 'neither of you clearly wins the 1v1' and late says the lane result 'rarely matters' because Ornn is a stat battery. Separately, the packet reports 54.81% over 374 games while MC_WR_TABLES.trundle.ornn reads 47.49 — a seven-point disagreement on the same matchup.
audit.why: A stage labelled for Ornn cannot be justified by a sentence saying neither side clearly wins; Skill is the value the prose supports. The win-rate conflict is more serious because the two numbers sit on opposite sides of even and the whole chart shape depends on which is right — 54.81% would make this one of Trundle's better lanes, 47.49 one of his worse. I have not touched the enums or written any claim that depends on the headline figure.
audit.corrected: win[6] should read Skill, matching whys[6]. The win-rate source conflict needs resolving before the rest of the chart can be judged.

audit.why: The packet flagged 'Searing Charges' in the mid paragraph as a probable wrong ability name. It is a false positive — Searing Charge is Ornn's E and the string was simply using it as a verb. It also flagged 'Use Pillar of Ice' and 'Land Volcanic Rupture' as near-misses; both are correct names.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 feel deceptively even and then Ornn takes over. At level 1 your Chomp bites his AD cleanly and the heal from minion deaths keeps you healthy, but Ornn's base armor is high enough that raw autos barely dent him — do not burn E or commit to a long trade before you have W. At level 2 drop Frozen Domain immediately if he steps up for a last-hit; the move speed and attack speed let you land two or three Chomps before he responds. The problem is level 3: the moment Ornn has Volcanic Rupture, Bellows Breath, and Searing Charge, he can brittle you, shove through, and knock you up in a sequence that out-damages your W healing. Stay ahead of the wave so you meet his ground-slam near your side, where you can sidestep the narrow Rupture and punish the whiff — missing Q is the one window you own in this window.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 feel deceptively even and then Ornn takes over. At level 1 Chomp bites his AD on a flat 3.5s and King's Tribute heals you off dying minions, but Living Forge gives him extra Armor and MR from every source, so raw autos barely dent him — do not commit long before you have W. At level 2 drop Frozen Domain the moment he steps up for a last-hit; the move and attack speed buy you two or three Chomps. The problem is level 3. Volcanic Rupture is 9s at 800 and leaves a magma pillar at the end of the fissure, Bellows Breath brittles you with its FINAL gout, and Searing Charge knocks up only when Ornn collides with terrain — the pillar is the setup, the charge is the payoff. Sidestep the narrow fissure and the sequence has nothing to detonate on.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 belong to Ornn in the lane, but level 6 is where the match flips in your favor for the rest of the game. At levels 4-5 he controls the slow-push, stacks brittle off Bellows Breath on the wave, and tanks trades that would lose for anyone else — respect the damage and farm safely rather than force trades into his full rotation. Do not use Pillar offensively here or he Searing Charges right through it; save E to deny his Rupture follow-up. At level 6 his Call of the Forge God is genuinely terrifying — the first hit applies brittle, the second knockup ends your combo if it connects — but the moment both hits land and his R is on cooldown, you activate Subjugate. One full Subjugate rotation strips roughly 30% of his armor and MR onto you; combined with Frozen Domain he simply cannot kill you fast enough to stop the drain. Do not R before the second knockup lands or you will be interrupted; flash the second hit if needed, then immediately chain R and run him through your W zone.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 belong to Ornn in the lane, but level 6 is where the match flips in your favour for the rest of the game. At 4-5 he controls the slow-push, brittles the wave with Bellows Breath on a 12s, and tanks trades nobody else survives — farm rather than force. The Pillar rule here runs against instinct: never place Pillar of Ice near him, because Searing Charge knocks up when Ornn collides with TERRAIN and your own pillar is terrain. You would be handing him the wall his own Volcanic Rupture normally has to build first. At 6, Call of the Forge God is 140/120/100 against Subjugate's 120/100/80, so yours returns twenty seconds sooner at every rank. Its first pass damages, slows and brittles; only the recast knocks up. Let that recast resolve, then cast Subjugate — it takes a percentage of his Health, Armor and MR and doubles the theft over four seconds, and Living Forge has inflated all three.

edits.before: The lane result rarely matters because Subjugate makes Ornn a walking stat battery in every team fight. A tanky Ornn with Sunfire, Iceborn, and Warmog is the best possible target for your ultimate — you borrow all of it. Focus on being the front line who ults the enemy front line: walk into their formation, R the tankiest target (Ornn if he engages), and let the drain make you impossible to kill while your team follows. The only way this goes wrong late is if Ornn's Call of the Forge God upgrades your teammates' items into a strength they didn't need and his team scales past yours — win before the 30-minute forge advantage compounds, and never fight into Ornn's ult without your R available as an immediate answer.
edits.after: The lane result rarely matters, because Subjugate makes Ornn a walking stat battery in every team fight. Living Forge gives him extra Armor and MR from every source, so a Sunfire-Iceborn-Warmog Ornn is the richest target on the map for an ultimate that takes a percentage of Health, Armor and MR and doubles it over four seconds. Be the front line who ults their front line: walk in, R the tankiest body, let the theft carry the fight. Your timing edge is real — 120/100/80 against his 140/120/100 means you arrive at the next fight with R first. The failure case is letting his forge advantage compound across the map, so close the game before it does.

notes: BIGGEST CORRECTION: mid said 'Do not use Pillar offensively here or he Searing Charges right through it.' Searing Charge does the opposite of going through terrain — it detonates on it: 'If Ornn collides with terrain while charging, the impact creates a shockwave... and knocks up enemies.' Pillar of Ice is impassable terrain, so a pillar near Ornn hands him the wall his own Volcanic Rupture usually has to build first. The conclusion (hold Pillar) was accidentally right; the stated reason was backwards, which is worse, because a player who tests it will see the charge stop at the pillar, conclude the entry was wrong, and start casting it. SECOND ADD: Volcanic Rupture is named eight times without anyone saying it leaves a magma pillar at the end of the fissure. That pillar is the terrain half of his combo — naming it turns 'wall-knockup setup' into 'watch where the fissure ends'. Brittle also comes specifically from Bellows Breath's FINAL gout, so walking out through the front of the breath avoids it. THIRD ADD: Living Forge, absent from both layers, gives Ornn extra Armor and MR from ALL sources — which is the mechanism behind the entry's central late-game claim that he is the best Subjugate target in the game, previously asserted with no reason attached. COOLDOWNS: Call of the Forge God 140/120/100 against Subjugate 120/100/80 — Trundle's is back twenty seconds sooner at every rank, which is what actually makes 'level 6 flips the match' true. Also corrected the ultimate's shape: the first pass damages, slows and brittles, and only the recast knocks up, so there is one knockup to survive rather than two. REMOVED AN UNSOURCED NUMBER: mid claimed 'One full Subjugate rotation strips roughly 30% of his armor and MR'. No percentage appears in the kit file, so I replaced it with the doubling-over-four-seconds behaviour Riot does state. UNVERIFIED, LEFT ALONE: what Brittle actually does. whys[2] and wants.foe[0] described it as a 'percent-HP conversion'; Riot's text for Bellows Breath and Call of the Forge God says only that enemies 'become Brittle' without defining it, so I removed the percent-HP claim rather than restating it and made no substitute claim. WIN-RATE CONFLICT: packets/trundle.json says 54.81% over 374 games; MC_WR_TABLES.trundle.ornn says 47.49. Those straddle even and the chart shape depends on which is authoritative — see questionsForUser. NOT EDITED (enum): win[6] reads Ornn above a whys[6] that says neither side clearly wins the 1v1.
